negative_anchors: b5644f8: argument position alone does not explain candidate silence
a4eea29: lexical realization does not explain candidate silence (YES 22/22 across L1-L4)
purpose: Test whether Candidate Generation loses a known, already-covered lexical trigger when syntactic complexity increases. Lexical trigger held constant: YES=provide, NO=deny.

conditions.C0: canonical baseline (finite, local, single-clause, canonical double-object)
conditions.C1: intervening material / argument distance (identical adjunct everywhere)
conditions.C2: complex subject (subject relative clause; target stays finite and local)
conditions.C4: embedded finite target clause (target inside finite relative clause; matrix holds another event)
conditions.C5: nonfinite target clause (participial; semantically asserted; evaluated as own condition)

material_shape: 4 semantic subtypes x 6 conditions x YES/NO = 48 sentences / 24 YES-NO pairs; same triplets across C0-C5; pair differs only in verb
invariants: same lexical YES trigger provide and NO trigger deny everywhere
no pronouns/anaphora (matrix tails use definite article, not possessives)
no modality, no negation, no conditionals, no metaphors

interpretation.flat_YES_recall: weakens hypothesis that ordinary syntactic complexity explains batch-6 FNs
interpretation.NO_rise: not a failure per se (candidate stage intentionally assertionsblind); relevant only as interaction effect
